Handling Outliers Just assume for now you are given dataset as in image below
with lot other features that can conclusively help determine "Overall" runs
saved. How will you handle second row (Ravindra Jadeja) considering Matches is
one of important feature along with others like past runs saved, fitness
level, fielding position etc Will you treat the second row as a) Outlier and
drop the instance b) Outlier and do some specific treatment, if so what c)
Leave the data as it is and train the model (Assume natural data pattern) d)
Check if it is data/reporting issue e) Check this feature in combination with
other features (multivariate analysis/engineering) f) Reduce the impact of
outlier Coming to Outliers in general, not all outliers typically stand out.
Take in many cases fraudulent transaction might look very genuine. Amplify
this with huge dataset and large features space, making it even more complex
to handle outliers. In some case even seasonality or natural drift might look
as outlier Outlier needs closer look at business and data and can be handled
with options mentioned above depending on the nature of outlier. Dig deeper
into it as much as possible hashtag#datascience hashtag#outliers

Roger Federer vs Novak Djokovic Wimbledon final just started. Have you ever
wondered inspite of so many young talents coming in for last 16 years what
gets the top 3 seed (Federer, Nadal, Djokovic) always in Wimbledon final
(Except for one year) In recent interview 4th seeded Kevin Anderson brought
some interesting facts below "It's not lack of quality other players, They
(Top 3) know what it's like playing on Center Courts week in, week out at the
Grand Slams. They know what it's like being in the semis, in the finals. That
sort of experience just keeps on compounding, Nobody can simulate what it
feels like going out and playing the finals of a Grand Slam, semis and finals"
Above is true with any domain even though if not direct correlation.
Experience keeps on compounding. Experience tells organization on what will
work and what will not and if works what is the best way it will work. Sad
reality in industries like software engineering, experience is looked at as
liabilities rather asset. I see lot of posts on Age discrimination in
LinkedIn. To add to the fact 80% of workforce in silicon valley is under the
age of 32 years Recruiters and hiring managers should test ones knowledge or
capability rather testing ones ability to do work based on Age. hashtag#age
